source_text: OK; so what I am wondering is whether tasks like "read and analyse all of Joe's circa-5000 turns" would hammer futon1b in a way that makes it unusable or whether these kinds of queries are now safe

fragments.text: OK; so what I am wondering is whether tasks like "read and analyse all of Joe's circa-5000 turns" would hammer futon1b in a way that makes it unusable or whether these kinds of queries are now safe

reply_text:
㊥ Gist: Reading and analysing your roughly 5,000 turns doesn't load futon1b at all. The 象 readers work from turn files already on disk and write their readings to disk too, so the store is only touched when the turns are first harvested, which takes a few seconds in pages. The cases that have actually hurt futon1b are different ones: bulk writes, and one unbounded deep health check.

㊬ (what I measured this turn)
- **Paged reads:** a page of 1,000 of your turns took 0.07–0.40 s, about 2 MB each. Today's harvests were 4 pages for your turns since 21 September and 7 for the start records. Neither caused trouble.
- **Memory:** futon1b's heap is at 2.7 of 4 GB. Its health page shows a concurrency limit, with 2 query slots free when I looked.
- **The backfill itself:** `backfill_pack.py` and `session_turn_analysis.py` contain no network calls. The packs are built from the turn files under `storage/operator-turns/`, and the readings are written back there. So the four seats reading now cost the Kimi and Codex seats their time, not futon1b.

㊟ (what is still unsafe)
- **Bulk writes:** about 330 mission-file rewrites on 30 September set off around 9 times as many store writes. That led to timeouts and a nearly full heap, and every Agency job was blocked while the store was busy.
- **Deep health check:** `/health?deep=true` pushed a nearly full heap into an out-of-memory exit on 23 August.
- **Unpaged queries:** the entities endpoint stops at 5,000 rows and offers no way to page past that. A query without `limit` or a date range asks the store for far more than it needs.

A read of your turns stays safe if it pages by date with `limit=1000`, as all of today's harvests did. Running several full-history sweeps at the same moment hasn't been tested.

🈖 (why the Minard extraction was slower) It took 6m24s because it pulled every pattern retrieval in the window, 20,306 rows over 21 pages, as well as 5,786 rows of your turns. That still means a few minutes of paged reads, not a load that stops the store working. The comparison job that's on hold would read the Minard results and the 象 readings from disk, so it needn't query futon1b at all.
